gloss: Used to form the superlative of adjectives and adverbs.
Used to form the second-person singular present tense and past tense of verbs. (if thou is the subject; not used with you)
A person or thing that does an action indicated by the root verb; used to form an agent noun.
A person or thing to which the root verb is done or can be done satisfactorily.
A person whose occupation is the root noun; (more broadly, occasionally with adjectives) a person characterized by the root.
A person or thing to which a certain number or measurement applies.
More; used to form the comparative.
More; used to form the comparative.
Added to transitive verbs to form words meaning a person or thing that is the object of that verb (i.e., to whom or to which an action is done).
Added to intransitive verbs to form words meaning a person or thing that is the subject of that verb (that is, who or that does an action).
Used to form words meaning a person who is the other party to a contract or other transaction involving a person described by the corresponding word ending in -or.
Used to form words meaning a person who has undergone a particular medical procedure.
Used to form adjectives and nouns describing things and characteristics of a city, region, or country, such as the people and the language spoken by these people.
Used to form nouns meaning the jargon or language used by a particular profession or being or in a particular context.
Used to form female equivalents.
The wife of.

When attached to certain adjectives, it forms a transitive verb whose meaning is, to make (adjective). Usually, the verb is ergative, sometimes not. The same construction could also be done to certain (fewer) nouns, as, strengthen, in which case the verb means roughly, "to give (noun) to", or "to become like (noun)".
The surgical removal of.
In the style or manner of; appended to nouns, especially proper nouns, and forming adjectives.
Resembling; appended to nouns, especially proper nouns, and forming adjectives.
An unsaturated hydrocarbon having at least one double bond; an alkene.
An aromatic hydrocarbon based on benzene.
A polymer derived from an alkene.
Same as -ance; having the state or condition of.
Added to occupational etc. nouns to form other nouns meaning the "art, craft, or practice of."
Added to verbs to form nouns meaning "place of" (an art, craft, or practice).
Added to nouns to form other nouns meaning "a class, group, or collection of."
Added to nouns to form other nouns meaning "behavior characteristic of."
Indicating a fundamental unit in some kind of structure, chiefly linguistic structure.
Forms adjectives, usually from proper nouns.
Noun-forming suffix found in words of Greek origin meaning “place or building associated with a specific purpose or person” (indicated by the root word)
